chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from a man, from Salih ibn Maytham, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no man who gives false testimony against the property of a Muslim man in order to dispossess him, except that God writes for him in his place a deed toward the Fire.

key_terms.شَهَادَةُ الزُّورِ: False testimony/perjury — one of the gravest sins in Islamic law, explicitly forbidden in the Quran (22:30) and hadith
key_terms.صَكٌّ: A deed, document, or promissory note — here used metaphorically for a divine decree irrevocably assigning the perjurer to Hell
key_terms.لِيَقْطَعَهُ: To cut him off, to dispossess him — indicating the malicious intent behind the false testimony

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about bearing false witness against a Muslim's property?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) declares that bearing false witness (shahada al-zur) to unlawfully seize a Muslim's property is a grave sin for which God records a guaranteed deed of entry into Hellfire. This hadith was transmitted in the context of the early Muslim community's concerns about the misuse of testimony in legal proceedings to dispossess the righteous of their wealth. The image of a 'deed to the Fire' (sakk ila al-nar) evokes the practice of written contracts, making the divine punishment concrete and irrevocable.
word_analysis: in order to cut him off (from it)

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from a man, from Salih Bin Maysam, 
Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘There is none from a man who testifies with a false testimony upon the wealth of a Muslim man in order to cut him off, except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Writes for him, a deed, for his place to the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ‘Uthman from a man from Salih ibn Mitham who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Whoever presents a false testimony against the assets of a Muslim man to cut off his ownership, for such witnessing Allah writes a certificate for him to the fire.’”
